topic: An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion
subject: religious-studies

items.q: Does the cosmological argument prove God exists beyond doubt?
items.correct: No — it is a reasoned argument with recognised strengths and criticisms.
items.random_wrong: It argues that God does not exist.
items.why: Philosophers debate such arguments rather than treating them as settled proof.

items.q: Does the problem of evil completely disprove God?
items.correct: No — it is a serious challenge to which believers offer responses (theodicies).
items.misconception: Yes, it settles the question entirely.
items.why: The problem of evil is debated; it doesn't conclusively settle the issue either way.

items.q: Are religious experiences accepted as proof by everyone?
items.correct: No — they convince some but are debated and open to other explanations.
items.misconception: Yes, everyone accepts them as proof.
items.random_wrong: They are never discussed in philosophy.
items.why: Religious experience is treated as evidence by some and questioned by others.
